analysis: What changed vs the 4 AM brief: the rebound is intact but cooling off its peak — Nasdaq-100 futures have narrowed from +2.87% at 4:23 AM ET to +2.23% by 6:42 AM ET, S&P from +1.98% to +1.64%, and Nvidia from +4.7% to +3.6% premarket. The move is still broad (AI hardware basket +5.8% on average, all ten names TECHi tracks above Wednesday's close; megacaps +1% to +3%+), but the fade from the peak on a thin half-day session is the tell: dip-buyers returned after the holiday, not a resolution of the AI-profitability, financing and circular-funding questions XTB flagged. The one real decliner is Vertex (-7.3%) on a regulatory delay, not a rejection — a stock-specific story in an otherwise risk-on tape. Oil is the second front with more detail now: the Jazan refinery projectile strike killed a worker and halted some operations, and two tankers hit mines near Hormuz, pushing Brent toward $97.30 and WTI +2.6% vs Wednesday's close ahead of Sunday's OPEC+ meeting. Gold (+4.8%) and silver (+9-10%) are still surging alongside equities, and the VIX has cooled to ~25.3 from Wednesday's 28.29 cash close but stays well above its ~19.5 long-term average. No qualifying Hacker News or Reddit threads added signal beyond the headlines, so community_signals is empty. Cash markets closed Thursday for Thanksgiving; today is a 1 PM ET early close, and the 8:30 AM ET trade/inventories data plus Black Friday sales reads are the day's only fresh macro inputs.
disclaimer: Not financial advice — for informational purposes only.

headlines.headline: US index futures narrowed from their early-morning peak but stayed sharply higher into the Black Friday half session: at 6:42 AM ET, Nasdaq-100 +2.23%, S&P 500 +1.64%, Dow +1.29% (Reuters) — down from +2.87%, +1.98% and +1.33% at 4:23 AM ET. At 6:08 AM ET the reads were Nasdaq +2.45%, S&P +1.80%, Dow +1.40%.
headlines.why_it_matters: The rebound is real but fading off its peak before the open — on a thin half-day session, that drift is the thing to watch, not the headline gain.

headlines.headline: Nvidia cooled to +3.6% premarket by 6:42 AM ET (from +4.7% at 4:23 AM ET), still ~37% below its October record high on its $149.30 Wednesday close; TECHi had it at $155.52 (+4.2%) at 5:44 AM ET. The AI hardware basket averaged +5.8% premarket: Marvell +8.0%, CoreWeave +7.4%, Micron +7.0%, AMD +4.4-5.3%, Broadcom +3.4-4.1%, TSMC +3.3%. Anthropic was up 4%+ premarket, back above its $83 IPO price.
headlines.why_it_matters: The bounce is concentrated in the same beaten-down AI names — a relief rally on cheaper valuations, not a resolution of the governance, export-curb and AI-financing worries; Huang's congressional hearings are Dec 1 (House) and Dec 3 (Senate).

headlines.headline: Megacaps rose together premarket (Finnhub quotes ~7:37 AM ET): Meta $629.67 (+3.24% vs Wednesday's $609.89 close), Tesla $388.07 (+2.09% vs $380.14), Microsoft $498.54 (+1.76% vs $489.93), Apple $358.95 (+0.95% vs $355.58); Amazon +3%+ and Alphabet Class A +2%+ in the 4:04 AM ET MSX.COM snapshot.
headlines.why_it_matters: A broad risk-on tape, not a single-name story — the hyperscalers that fund the AI buildout are bouncing with the chip names, which is what a durable rebound needs to look like.

headlines.headline: Vertex Pharmaceuticals fell ~7.3% in after-hours/premarket trading after the FDA extended its review of kidney drug povetacicept by up to three months, moving the decision date from Nov 30, 2026 to no later than Feb 28, 2027, after classifying Vertex's late-cycle response as a major amendment. Shares were ~$523-525 vs the $564.12 Wednesday close, erasing ~$10B in market value; rival Vera Therapeutics jumped ~17%.
headlines.why_it_matters: A delay, not a rejection — but it pushes a key approval catalyst past year-end, and Vertex is the one notable decliner in an otherwise risk-on tape.

headlines.headline: Oil kept climbing on Middle East supply threats: Brent ~$97.30 (+0.8%) and WTI ~$85.85 (+2.6% vs Wednesday's close) by mid-morning GMT, on track to snap a three-week losing streak. A projectile struck Saudi Aramco's 400k b/d Jazan refinery Thursday, killing one worker and halting some operations, a day after Houthi claims on Ras Tanura; Iran's Revolutionary Guards said two tankers hit sea mines near Oman's Khasab port in the Strait of Hormuz. OPEC+ meets Sunday on 2027 output policy.
headlines.why_it_matters: A supply-threat premium is building in energy into the OPEC+ meeting — a second front that can cut against the equity rebound if it escalates.

headlines.headline: Black Friday demand reads are set: the National Retail Federation forecasts November-December sales up 4.2% to $1.013 trillion, and Adobe forecasts $12.9B in US online Black Friday spending (+9.2% y/y) and $15.1B on Cyber Monday (+6.2%).
headlines.why_it_matters: Adobe's actual Black Friday and Cyber Monday tallies, against its forecasts, are the first real demand read for consumer-discretionary names this holiday season.

usac.why_it_matters: No fresh USAC company news overnight. Carry-forward: Q3 2026 (Nov 3) revenue $357.2M (+43% y/y) beat the ~$344.7M consensus and adjusted EPS $0.33 beat the $0.26 consensus; adjusted EBITDA $197.3M, DCF $127.1M, coverage 1.67x; FY26 adjusted EBITDA guidance narrowed to $770-780M and DCF to $495-505M; $0.525/unit quarterly distribution (annualized $2.10) paid Nov 6. Zacks raised FY2026 EPS estimate to $1.16 from $1.04 (Nov 24) and holds a Hold rating; a Nov 24 Zacks piece frames the growth case — $500M order book through 2029, >60% of 2027 new horsepower contracted, record $23.14/month revenue per horsepower (+8% y/y) — while a Nov 26 Seeking Alpha Hold note counters with limited upside at 8.29x forward EV/EBITDA amid substantial debt, against a Nov 25 buy-rated piece at $23.63 citing the 8.9% yield and 1.67x coverage. USAC opened Wednesday at $23.04. Next earnings Feb 16, 2027.
